terms.definition: Whether research gives a true picture of what is being studied.
terms.examiner: Interpretivists prize it. In Methods in Context answers, link validity to the particular group in the Item.

terms.definition: Whether the research can be repeated by another researcher and get the same results.
terms.examiner: Positivists prize it. Standardised methods such as structured questionnaires are reliable.

terms.definition: Whether the sample has the same characteristics as the wider group it is drawn from.
terms.examiner: Allows generalisation. Say what makes a particular sample unrepresentative, not just that it is.

terms.definition: Whether findings from a sample can be applied to the wider population.
terms.examiner: Depends on representativeness and sample size.

terms.definition: Turning a sociological concept into something that can be measured, such as defining class by occupation.
terms.examiner: Common in questions on questionnaires and official statistics.

terms.definition: The list of people from whom a sample is drawn, such as a school register.
terms.examiner: Problems: it may be out of date or exclude groups. Apply it to the Item's setting.

terms.definition: Finding participants by asking each one to put the researcher in touch with others.
terms.examiner: Used for hard-to-reach groups such as gang members. Not representative.

terms.definition: People changing their behaviour because they know they are being studied.
terms.examiner: A problem for overt observation and for lab experiments; covert observation avoids it.

terms.definition: The interviewer's presence, appearance or questions influencing the answers.
terms.examiner: Applies to interviews; contrast with the impersonal postal questionnaire.

terms.definition: Participants agreeing to take part after being told what the research involves and that they can withdraw.
terms.examiner: An ethical issue. With pupils, parents and schools must consent too: a strong application point.

terms.definition: Weber's term for understanding behaviour from the actor's point of view by putting yourself in their position.
terms.examiner: The goal of interpretivist methods such as participant observation and unstructured interviews.

terms.definition: Using more than one method or source to check findings.
terms.examiner: Shows methodological pluralism; useful in evaluation paragraphs.
